questions.question: What is a CLIA attack and how does the Context Bridge neutralize it?
questions.authoritative_context: A CLIA (Cross-Lineage / Cross-Instance Attack) occurs when an adversary captures an authentic, validly hashed finding from Session A and injects it into Session B with severed provenance. The Context Bridge checks the global_evidence_registry; if the finding originated in another session without a valid cross-session pointer, it is quarantined immediately as CROSS_SESSION_UNLINKED_REPLAY with a signed Merkle receipt and zero state pollution. Authenticated citations require verified source_session_id and source_node_id pointers in the active DAG.
ground_truth_claims: CLIA involves replaying authentic findings across session boundaries without lineage
Context Bridge checks global_evidence_registry for prior session ownership
Quarantines unlinked cross-session imports fail-closed
Requires verified source_session_id and source_node_id for authenticated citations
forbidden_hallucinations: accepts validly hashed findings regardless of session origin
